segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the three Apollonian Circles are the loci of points whose distances to two vertices of triangle A B C are in the inverse ratio of the adjacent sides: P B to P C equals c to b, P C to P A equals a to c, and P A to P B equals b to a.

segments.text: The A-Apollonian circle has diameter I a J a between the interior and exterior angle-bisector feet on side B C, and passes directly through vertex A. All three Apollonian circles belong to a coaxial pencil whose common chord is the Brocard axis.
